newsitem.title: ITALY: Seamless style shows there are no frills on Gucci.
newsitem.headline: Seamless style shows there are no frills on Gucci.

text.p: Italian fashion house Gucci unwrapped a seamless series of women's ready-to-wear designs on Thursday in a spare, unfrilly line-up of close-fitting tube dresses and knee-high suede boots.

In a his-and-hers display which included male models on the catwalk, deep chocolate brown, jade and mossy green as well as black dominated the 1997 spring/summer collection with outfits rarely more than a monochrome.

Strapless chocolate or black tube dresses, looking as if they were made from one continuous piece of material, were narrow and flat over the breast and hip but ruched into natural-looking folds at the waist, with the same design for evening in sparkling bronze and copper.

Skirts were tight at the hip and narrow, often stopping at the knee, while trousers too were tight at the hip, narrow-legged, split at the ankle to fit over boots and worn with bronze-coloured metal or articulated leather belts.
For footwear, models wore knee or ankle high suede boots in black or chocolate and jackets or coats in suede were often long, collarless and slit from the bottom into loose panels.
Knits were long sleeved and sliding off the shoulder or designed as camisole tops and crafted thin to be transparent.
A more luxuriant look came with velvety skirts and pencil strap dresses to below the knee, in bronze, a rich jungly green or jade which deepened into moss, or mottled red and black.

Summer tops included a chocolate brown halterneck which dropped in a continuous loop over either breast and was held in place by a belt threaded through at the waist and a thong across the lower back.

Gucci's hallmark metal circle appeared at one hip on a set of bikini bottoms and at the back of a brown tanga -- the female version of a man's g-string shown at the menswear summer collection earlier this year which a male model duly paraded again on Thursday.
The Milan shows move into their sixth day on Friday, with a little glamour in the shape of a few frills and plenty of leopardskin creeping into collections so far.
Designer Gianfranco Ferre offers up his latest designs along with fashion house Fendi on Friday, while Iceberg and Moschino are followed by Gianni Versace's main collection on Saturday.
Giorgio Armani, who displayed his younger Emporio Armani designs on Thursday, rounds the shows off with his primary collection on Sunday.
